definitions.dark: a one-photon block whose ideal algebra-mode probability p_algebra is 0: x y = 0, so the photon leaves only through the dilation ports and any algebra-mode detection is implementation error
definitions.bright: a one-photon block with p_algebra = 1: ||x y||^2 = 2, so the photon never reaches a dilation port
definitions.half: a strut, non-kite or four-label block with p_algebra = 1/2, independent of the signs s and t

preregistered.observable: per iteration phi = k pi/4, a(phi): the algebra-mode share of one-click samples in the block; the fit a(phi) = A + B cos(phi - phi0) over the eight iterations
preregistered.ideal: P(phi) = [4 + 2 cos phi (m00 m01 + m10 m11)] / 8: an edge block (job-00) follows (1 + cos phi)/2, bright at phi = 0 and dark at phi = pi; a strut block (job-01) is flat at 1/2 because m00 m01 + m10 m11 = 0; every iteration's per-mode ideal is exact over Q(sqrt2)
preregistered.hardware_report: fringe visibility B/A against 1 (edge) and 0 (strut), phase offset phi0, a_dark = a(pi) and a_bright = a(0) on one compiled mesh, with binomial intervals per iteration
preregistered.falsifier: on sim:belenos a fitted B more than 4.5 standard errors from 1/2 (edge) or 0 (strut); on qpu:belenos the edge-minus-strut visibility difference is the chip's zero-divisor contrast
preregistered.server: the job sends one ComputationIterator; a result without results_list, or one computed_circuit per iteration, shows how the platform executes iterations
